newsitem.title: CANADA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-GRETZKY REACHES 850 GOALS AS RANGERS BLANK LEAFS.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-GRETZKY REACHES 850 GOALS AS RANGERS BLANK LEAFS.

text.p: Wayne Gretzky scored his 850th career regular-season goal and Glenn Healy made 27 saves for his 11th career shutout as the New York Rangers blanked the Toronto Maple Leafs 4-0 on Saturday.

The Rangers, who survived a wild 6-5 shootout in New York on Friday against the Leafs, turned in a disciplined defensive effort to sweep the home-and-home series and extend their unbeaten streak to six games (5-0-1).
Healy faced just four shots in the first period, made 13 saves in the second and turned back seven third-period shots for his first shutout of the season.
"You have to give everybody credit tonight," said Healy. "We came in charged up and played just a solid hockey game."
Brian Noonan gave Healy all the offence he would need with a powerplay goal 6:40 into the game.

Gretzky, who scored twice on Friday, added his 13th of the season to make it 2-0 when he directed an Ulf Samuelsson shot past Felix Potvin at 6:49 of the second. It was the Great One's 54th goal in 58 career games against the Maple Leafs.

On Long Island, Tommy Salo made 24 saves for his second shutout in nine days and Bryan Smolinski's third-period goal snapped a scoreless tie as the New York Islanders blanked the Washington Capitals 2-0.
Salo recorded his first career shutout in another 2-0 win at Washington on November 29.
Niklas Andersson scored an empty net goal and assisted on Smolinski's tally 4:22 into the third.
At New Jersey, Darrin Shannon's goal 2:03 into overtime lifted the Phoenix Coyotes to a 4-3 victory over the Devils.
Phoenix, which also posted a 4-3 home overtime victory over New Jersey last month, has won four of its last five.
Shannon grabbed a rebound of a shot by defenceman Teppo Numminen that was stopped by Devils goaltender Martin Brodeur and flipped the puck into the top of the net.
Dallas Drake, who scored the game-tying goal for Dallas early in the third period, assisted on the game winner.
New Jersey lost despite outshooting Phoenix 35-17, including 14-1 in the second period.
In Montreal, Saku Koivu broke a 2-2 deadlock early in the third period as the Canadiens completed a home-and-home sweep of the Chicago Blackhawks with a 3-2 victory.

Koivu took a pass from Mark Recchi in the neutral zone and faked out defenceman Chris Chelios and goaltender Jeff Hackett before putting a wrist shot into the net 39 seconds into the final period for the game winner.

On his next shift, however, Koivu suffered a torn knee ligament and will be sidelined two months. Montreal's Marc Bureau also went down in the first period with torn ligaments in his right knee and will be out three months.
In Boston, Theo Fleury scored from behind the net with 1:48 left in the second period to lift the Calgary Flames into a 1-1 tie with the Bruins.

Fleury banked a shot into the net off Boston goaltender Bill Ranford to give Calgary its lone point in an 0-3-1 road trip. Sandy Moger scored Boston's lone goal on a powerplay seven minutes into the game.
Ranford finished with 35 saves, while Calgary netminder Trevor Kidd made 34 stops.

In Pittsburgh, Alex Hicks scored with 9:55 remaining to break a third-period tie and Patrick Lalime made 30 saves in his first NHL start as the Penguins rallied for a 5-3 win over the Anaheim Mighty Ducks.
Dmitri Mironov's two second-period goals put the Ducks in front 3-1. But Pittsburgh came back with four unanswered goals to extend their unbeaten streak to seven games.
Jaromir Jagr's empty-netter with 11 seconds left was his league-leading 27th goal.
In Hartford, Jeff O'Neill, Robert Kron and Kevin Dineen scored in a 2:45 span early in the third period to erase a two-goal deficit and give the Whalers a 6-4 win over the Buffalo Sabres.
Geoff Sanderson had two goals and two assists for the Northeast Division-leading Whalers.
Matthew Barnaby had a pair of goals for the Sabres, who led 4-2 after two periods.

In Los Angeles, Philippe Boucher and Steven Finn scored their first goals of the season less than two and a half minutes apart in the third period as the Kings handed the Colorado Avalanche a 4-2 defeat.
Brad Smyth and Dimitri Khristich also scored for Los Angeles as Colorado suffered consecutive losses for the first time since opening the season with two defeats.
In Vancouver, Alexandre Daigle scored just 31 seconds into the third period to help Ottawa snap a four-game losing streak as the Senators edged the Canucks 3-2.
Daigle's goal made it 3-1 after Steve Duchesne's controversial powerplay tally 4:57 into the second period broke a 1-1 tie.

The Canucks protested Duchesne's goal because goaltender Corey Hirsch felt he was deliberately pulled out of position by Daniel Alfredsson's stick. But Hirsch's arguement to referee Don Van Massenhoven fell on deaf ears.
In San Jose, Cory Cross scored his first goal of the season with 47 seconds remaining to lift the Tampa Bay Lightning to a 4-3 victory over the Sharks.

Cross took a pass from Patrick Poulin while breaking into the San Jose zone and fired a slap shot over diving defenceman Al Iafrate and through the pads of goaltender Kelly Hrudey for the game-winner.
Poulin also had a second-period short-handed goal to go along with his key assist for the Lightning. Ron Sutter had a pair of goals for the Sharks.
